brief.headline: Minnie's bathing and lower-body dressing independence has declined since the last review, and she is skipping showers because she fears slipping. Sertraline was started on 2026-11-13 for depressive symptoms.

items.statement: The OT ADL reassessment on 2026-10-11 found Minnie now needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing. She was independent at the last review. The OT recommends a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower, and more home care hours for bathing support.

questions_for_team: Can the tub transfer bench and handheld shower be put in place now, and should home care hours for bathing support be increased as the OT recommended? What is the plan for bathing in the meantime?
Is Minnie's fear of slipping, and the skipped showers, linked to her mood or to the new ADL needs? Does the team want a fall-risk or home safety review?
Who will complete the sertraline recheck due around 2026-12-11, and how will mood, side effects, and falls be monitored?
Should the flu vaccine be offered at the next visit?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and the last IDT review date so that all changes are compared against the correct baseline.
Falls and near-falls in the window: count, circumstances, injuries, and whether any fall occurred while on new sertraline or antihypertensive/beta-blocker therapy (metoprolol succinate).
ED visits and hospital admissions in the window, including any chest pain, cardiac, or bleeding presentations given ischemic heart disease and concurrent clopidogrel.
Bleeding or bruising review: any GI bleeding, melena, hematuria, epistaxis, or new anemia-related symptoms, and recent hemoglobin trend given anemia history and dual antiplatelet/SSRI exposure.

Medication reconciliation: duplicate statin entries (simvastatin 10 mg started 2026-04-20 and simvastatin 20 mg started 2026-03-23 both active); confirm which is intended, whether one was stopped, and whether the prescriber is aware of both.

Medication starts and stops in the window: sertraline 25 mg started 2026-11-13 for depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14); check adherence, early side effects (GI upset, sleep change, dizziness, hyponatremia signs), and that the follow-up plan is documented.
Mood and depression follow-up: repeat PHQ-9 or equivalent, suicidality screening, and whether the depressive symptoms were assessed for relation to Alzheimer's disease progression or social change.

Cognition trend: changes in memory, orientation, or executive function since the last review; any new confusion, medication-related delirium concerns, or caregiver-reported changes; confirm cognitive assessment is current.

Weight and BMI trend (obesity, prediabetes): recorded weights across the window, appetite and intake changes that could relate to depression or dementia, and glycemic screening status (HbA1c or fasting glucose) if due.

Blood pressure and cardiac symptoms: BP and heart rate trend on metoprolol, angina use of nitroglycerin spray (frequency since start), and lipid panel timing relative to statin changes; also confirm colon polyp surveillance follow-up is scheduled given the 2026-01-04 polyp diagnosis and clopidogrel use.
